# 📊 NBFC Daily Watch — Friday, November 27, 2026

Friday edition for 27 November 2026 (IST), covering Thursday 26 November to Friday morning; data compiled 07:00–07:45 IST. Today is a normal trading day — the NSE holiday master, read 07:02 IST, has no entry for 27-Nov-2026 in any segment, and the next equity-segment holiday is 25 December 2026. **Every index and stock figure below is Thursday 26 November's close**, from the NSE's own files for the date; the Sensex is a BSE index and is cited to ET Now, never the NSE archive. IBJA's headline block this morning still reads "Rates will be uploaded soon" — a normal session not yet posted at the 07:02 read — so the domestic benchmark below is the **26 November PM session, labelled as such**. **AGLOC's block is dated 27 November 2026 — today's — and it rises ₹124 on yesterday's block**, on a fresh reference. **A US calendar fact governs the metals rows:** 26 November was US Thanksgiving, and CME Group's holiday notice states it will not derive or disseminate settlement prices for CME, CBOT, NYMEX or COMEX that day — **there is no Comex settlement dated 26 November**; the last is 25 November's, and every 26 November figure below is labelled for what it is. Friday is a two-report day — news and regulation; the weekly analysis desk files on Mondays, and nothing weekly is due today.

## 🔴 URGENT / High Impact

### The warnings became actions: legal auction notices are out, and lenders have told the RBI they are writing fresh loans at 60–65% LTV
Through Wednesday, this cycle's record was warnings and monitoring — the RBI's 23 November meeting with NBFC and HFC chief executives, the reported step-up in portfolio reporting, and Wednesday's first margin-call report. **Thursday is the day the warnings became actions, and three outlets reported it within 24 hours.** The Economic Times (Sangita Mehta, ET Bureau, last updated 26 November, 05:30 IST) reports that **gold finance companies have started issuing legal auction notices**, and — in ET's own sourcing, people with knowledge of the matter — **thresholds were breached in nearly 40% of gold-loan portfolios at such financiers, with the ratio crossing 95% in some cases**. The notices require borrowers to **repay part of the loan or pledge additional collateral**, failing which the pledged jewellery may be auctioned; **gold auctions are held 30 days after serving a legal notice**. ET states the mechanic plainly: **in the gold-loan business an LTV breach is deemed a default by the borrower even where no repayment obligation has been missed**, and margin calls are reaching a "sizable customer base" **for the first time in about four years**.

The number that matters most in Thursday's reporting is a representation, not a rule: **banks and gold-loan companies such as Muthoot and Manappuram have informed the RBI that, as a prudential measure, they have lowered the LTV on fresh loans to an average of 60–65% from about 75%** (ET's sources). **ET writes "Muthoot" without saying which entity, and this report keeps ET's wording exactly: Muthoot Finance is the listed company; Muthoot Fincorp is not named in the report, and nothing in it is attributed to Muthoot Fincorp.** The standing bands are unchanged — **85% for loans up to ₹2.5 lakh, 80% for ₹2.5–5 lakh, 75% above ₹5 lakh** — and a representation to the RBI is not a rule change: what ET reports is lenders *informing* the regulator of where they are writing fresh business, written here as reported, not as a requirement.

The scale behind the notices is CRIF's, via ET: **the gold-loan portfolio expanded to about ₹23 lakh crore as of 30 September 2026, roughly 12% of the ₹185 lakh crore retail-loan market**. Two of ET's own market citations need their labels stated: its IBJA reference — 999 at **₹1,21,038 per 10 g on a rolling one-month basis, against evening closing rates of ₹1,41,710 on 26 October 2026** — is **IBJA's 25 November PM print, not a 26 November figure**; IBJA's 26 November PM 999 is ₹1,22,641, the benchmark used below. And ET's "$3,481" international price, via investing.com, is an **intraday reference print, not a Comex settlement** — the last settlement on the record is 25 November's $3,534.70 — and stays out of the settlement record.

BusinessLine (Ashokamithran T, updated 26 November, 20:41 IST) reports the same turn from inside the lenders: **gold-loan companies are shifting focus from growth to collections** after the price fall pushed LTVs higher. Industry executives put the arithmetic in numbers: **portfolio LTVs at some gold-loan-focused NBFCs have crossed 75%, and certain segments may have breached 85%**; **loans originated at 80–85% LTV after the RBI relaxed norms for lower-ticket loans have jumped to 90–95%** after the correction. A senior executive at a leading gold-loan company, unnamed, is quoted directly: **"My full effort right now is into collections. Growth is not happening. In November, I am not focused on growth at all. The focus is reducing the LTV and collections."** Companies have started offering **interest-rate rebates and other incentives** to keep borrowers servicing. **Parth Gutka of 360 ONE Capital**: "Loans that originated at over 60 per cent LTV have now reached 75 per cent and this would roughly be half of the overall gold loan portfolio" — NBFCs more vulnerable than banks, he adds. **Piran Engineer, Senior Research Analyst at CLSA India**, expects stress to start surfacing **as early as the December quarter**, with lenders demanding additional collateral and repayments; executives see fresh business taking a back seat until collateral values stabilise.

Business Today (Amit Mudgill, 26 November, 10:36 IST) carries Antique Stock Broking's scenario analysis, in Antique's own words: **"Gold prices have corrected 30 per cent from their January 2026 peak, and our analysis suggests that loans disbursed in 1QFY27 have nearly breached the regulatory LTV limit at current prices. A further 21 per cent correction in gold prices across the loan tenure could result in recovery losses on slippages from the 1QFY27 disbursement vintage."** Antique calls that further decline "very steep" and **limits the risk to loans with tenures exceeding six months**. It names the structure now showing up in the books: **the shift from bullet repayments to monthly EMIs is contributing to higher Stage 2/3 assets in Q2FY27**, a near-term headwind expected to normalise over the next couple of quarters. The historical comparison is FY21, when gold corrected 15% between August 2020 and February 2021: **recovery rates were 84% for Muthoot, 95% for Manappuram and 99% for IIFL Finance, with no major credit-cost spike**. **"Muthoot" in Antique's series is Muthoot Finance, the listed company — not Muthoot Fincorp.** Antique's ratings, reported as the brokerage's view: **Manappuram 'Buy', target cut to ₹370; Muthoot Finance 'Hold', target ₹2,650** — it prefers Manappuram. Those are calls on two listed peers, not on this company.

The three correction figures in circulation on 26 November do not agree, and this report does not blend them: **ET puts the fall at 35% from the January peak, and 11% in November so far; Antique puts it at 30% from the January 2026 peak; BusinessLine puts it at nearly 19% from their January peaks.** They measure different reference points and are not reconcilable from the sources in this pack. Each figure carries its outlet's name; none is picked and none is blended.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: the mechanism ET, BusinessLine and Antique describe — legal notices, part-repayment, additional collateral, auction 30 days after a notice, an LTV breach deemed a default without a missed repayment — is the ongoing-LTV maintenance that applies across gold-loan lenders, including Muthoot Fincorp, and the collections-over-growth shift is described by industry executives, not by any named company. No public document states how many such notices the company has sent, where its book sits against the bands, or what share of its portfolio originated above 60% LTV; ET's nearly-40% figure is an industry-level characterisation from unnamed sources and belongs to ET. Nothing here is asserted about the company's own book.
Sources: [Economic Times, Sangita Mehta, 26 Nov 05:30 IST](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/banking/finance/banking/gold-crash-triggers-auction-notices-as-ltv-breaches-hit-lenders/articleshow/136172114.cms) · [BusinessLine, Ashokamithran T, 26 Nov 20:41 IST](https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/markets/gold/gold-loan-growth-slows-as-falling-gold-prices-push-lenders-into-collection-mode/article71746853.ece) · [Business Today, Amit Mudgill, 26 Nov 10:36 IST](https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/story/manappuram-muthoot-finance-shares-gold-prices-fall-what-scenario-analysis-indicates-569598-2026-11-26)

### The 26 November session: the Nifty rose and the NBFC complex was sold — except the two large gold-loan names
The broad market rose on Thursday and the lending complex was sold. The **Nifty 50 closed at 25,884.50, up 65.25 points or 0.25%**; Nifty Midcap 100 added 0.32% to 61,781.85, Nifty Smallcap 100 0.74% to 19,372.15; **India VIX closed at 16.84, the NSE file's own printed change −0.84 points or −4.73%**. The **Sensex — a BSE index, not in the NSE archive — closed at 84,328.59, up 390.31 points or 0.46%** (ET Now, 26 November 16:04 IST; corroborated by Bajaj Broking's closing bell and TOI's live blog, which records the intraday high of 84,551.74).

The divergence is the story. **Nifty NBFC fell 1.73% to 55,355.50 — down 972.17 points — on a day the Nifty rose 0.25%**; Nifty Bank closed 63,535.30, down 0.26%, and Nifty Financial Services 28,718.90, down 0.16%. Money moved out of lenders on a day the broad index rose, and inside the NBFC set the split ran along one line: **Muthoot Finance rose 0.33% to ₹2,558.00 and Manappuram 0.93% to ₹270.00 while the NBFC index fell 1.73%** — the two largest listed gold financiers were bought while the wider lending complex was sold. The falls: **IIFL Finance −2.71% to ₹593.95; Shriram Finance −2.84% to ₹961.85; Bajaj Finance −2.96% to ₹1,097.85; Cholamandalam −1.34% to ₹1,842.90; M&M Financial −2.43% to ₹285.35; Five Star −2.66% to ₹413.25; Aditya Birla Capital −2.01% to ₹413.50; PNB Housing −1.04% to ₹1,171.00; HDB Financial −1.10% to ₹551.70. Muthoot Microfin rose 3.53% to ₹164.45.**

What that pattern is and is not: a comparison of ticker moves on one session — the session after the auction-notice reporting broke — not evidence about any single book; no public document ties any single close to any single lender's collateral position. **Muthoot Finance is a listed peer, not Muthoot Fincorp; Muthoot Microfin is a listed group company, not Muthoot Fincorp either; every price above belongs to the company whose ticker printed it.**

The flows ran with the broad index, not the lenders: **FII/FPI net +₹5,843.33 crore** (bought ₹17,879.74 crore, sold ₹12,036.41 crore) and **DII net +₹5,630.72 crore** (bought ₹24,352.87 crore, sold ₹18,722.15 crore) — NSE provisional, combined +₹11,474.05 crore; final FPI numbers from NSDL can differ. CNBC TV18's framing: **FIIs extended their buying streak to 18 consecutive sessions on Thursday** — the streak count is CNBC TV18's, not computed here.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none directly. Muthoot Fincorp is unlisted and has no share price in either index, and the divergence is a comparison of index and ticker moves, not evidence about any single lender's book.

### Gold turns up — the 25 November down-session is reversed — and AGLOC's ceiling rises with it
The domestic benchmark turned up. IBJA's **26 November PM session — the latest posted at the 07:02 IST read — put 999 at ₹1,22,641 per 10 g (₹12,264.10 a gram) and 916 at ₹1,12,339 (₹11,233.90 a gram)**, against 25 November PM prints of ₹1,21,038 and ₹1,10,871: **+₹1,603 (+1.32%) on 999 and +₹1,468 (+1.32%) on 916 — a rise that ends the single down-session of 25 November** (the 916 PM series ran ₹1,13,486 on 20 November, ₹1,14,450 on 23 November, ₹1,10,871 on 25 November and ₹1,12,339 now — up, down, up; 23 November was itself a rise, so this reverses one down-session, not two). 24 November was a market holiday — IBJA's own 30-day PDF row reads "24-Nov-26 Market Holiday" — so 23 → 25 → 26 November are the consecutive sessions. **Silver 999 rose ₹4,402 (+3.08%) to ₹1,47,347 a kg.** Within the day, the PM session sat **below** the AM on gold — 999, **−₹341 (−0.28%)**; 916, **−₹313 (−0.28%)** — and **above** it on silver: **+₹414 (+0.28%)**.

The international record has a hole today, stated rather than papered over: **26 November was US Thanksgiving, and CME Group's own holiday notice says it will not derive or disseminate settlement prices for CME, CBOT, NYMEX or COMEX that day.** **There is no Comex settlement dated 26 November, and none is written here.** The last settlement is 25 November's: **front-month Comex gold settled at $3,534.70 an ounce, down 0.71%** (Dow Jones Market Data Data Talk, 25 November; the Data Talk series publishes on a 13:52 ET / 18:52 GMT wire clock, the timestamp its 24 November edition carries), **$25.20 below the prior settlement of $3,559.90** — and both closes are on the record in Dow Jones's own 24 November Data Talk, which reported the $3,559.90 settlement as a $89.30, or 2.45%, loss. Silver is the same structure: **front-month silver settled at $40.052, down 70.80 cents or 1.74% — a new 52-week low and the lowest settlement since 28 August 2025** (Dow Jones Data Talk, 25 November). CME's own delivery report confirms the November 2026 COMEX gold contract settled at $3,534.70 on the 25 November intent date. A 26 November **futures daily bar** does exist and is labelled for what it is: **gold $3,593.40, +$57.60, +1.63%, range $3,578.80–$3,634.70**, and **silver $41.750, +4.24%** — daily bars on a session CME did not settle, never settlements. Business Standard's intraday "near $3,575" print is an intraday reference, not a settlement, and stays out of the settlement record.

**AGLOC's block is dated 27 November 2026 — today's — and it rises ₹124 at the 85% band on yesterday's block: ₹9,548 a gram at 85% LTV, ₹8,987 at 80% and ₹8,425 at 75%, on a jewellery reference of ₹11,233.** Against the 26 November block (₹9,424 / ₹8,869 / ₹8,315 on ₹11,087), that is **+₹124 at the 85% band, +₹118 at 80%, +₹110 at 75%, with the reference up ₹146**. The reference is fresh, not carried forward: **₹11,233 is IBJA's 26 November PM 916 rate ÷ 10 (11,233.9)**, so today's block rests on Thursday afternoon's print exactly as the 26 November block rested on the 25 November one. **All three bands move together because they are fixed percentages of the one reference — one observation, not three** — and the percentages on those changes are arithmetic on AGLOC's own two blocks, because the page states rupee figures only.

On the domestic exchange, the quote board rose with the benchmark: **MCX GOLD 04DEC2026 at ₹1,22,272 per 10 g, up ₹1,135 or 0.94%, and MCX SILVER 04DEC2026 at ₹1,45,843 a kg, up ₹3,326 or 2.33%** — quote-board daily-bar prices, not exchange settlements, and no rupee change is derived from them for any other contract. Business Standard's intraday report corroborates the opens — gold ₹1,603 higher at 1,22,740, silver ₹3,283 higher at 1,45,800.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: the operative AGLOC ceiling for today is **₹9,548 at the 85% band, ₹124 above yesterday's** — the second upward move in the published ceiling since 17 November, after the one on 24 November (₹9,646 → ₹9,728), and it applies on every ticket size at once. The ceiling applies across lenders; no Muthoot Fincorp-specific figure is in any public document, and none is inferred.

### The rupee gives back 24 paise as Brent settles above $96 — the import bill moves the currency that prices the gold
The rupee settled **24 paise lower at 92.44 against the US dollar (provisional) on Thursday** (PTI via The Hindu, 26 November 16:16 IST) — against a prior close the outlets do not agree on: **PTI puts Wednesday at 92.20, the highest level this fiscal year; Business Standard (23:04 IST) puts it at 92.24.** The 4-paise disagreement is stated, not resolved; yesterday's edition's figure is not restated. Reuters via Business Recorder has the close 0.2% lower at **92.4450**. The intraday range was **92.31–92.66 (PTI; Business Standard 92.33–92.66)**, from an open of 92.50; the rupee has recovered nearly 5% from its lowest-ever close of 96.88 on 8 October (PTI). The dollar index stood at 103.70 (PTI), and the **10-year G-sec yield rose 7 bps to 7.24%** (Business Standard).

Oil is why the currency gave back ground, and this one settled. **Front-month ICE Brent for January delivery settled at $96.57 a barrel, up $1.96 or 2.07%** (Dow Jones Market Data, 26 November 20:10, via Morningstar), on **Houthi claims of hitting Saudi Arabia's largest refinery and Iranian claims of mines striking ships in the Strait of Hormuz** (Reuters via Euronext, confirming the $96.57 and the $1.96). One Reuters copy describes the rise as 1.2% where Dow Jones gives 2.07% on the same $1.96; the dollar figures agree, and this report gives Dow Jones's 2.07% with the $1.96 stated. **WTI did not settle — the US Thanksgiving holiday** (Reuters); it was $84.84, up $1.16 or 1.39%, at 13:21 ET — an intraday print, not a settlement.

The connection is mechanism, not forecast: **this oil move is the direct input to India's import bill, the import bill moves the rupee, and the rupee is the same currency that prices the domestic gold benchmark above.** Nothing here predicts either market's next move.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none directly. The rupee and the oil price set the currency backdrop to the collateral arithmetic; nothing in this section is a forecast of either.

## 🏛️ RBI & Regulatory — Headlines Only

### Nothing dated 26 or 27 November changes a lending rule; the RBI's newest blocks are liquidity operations and a sanctions-list update
**No RBI, SEBI or IBBI instrument dated 26 or 27 November changes a rule that applies to Muthoot Fincorp's lending business.** The RBI's press-release list, read 07:02 IST, has its newest block at 26 November, and it is all liquidity operations and statistical releases — VRR auctions and their results, Reserve Money and Money Supply for the fortnight ended 15 November, a conversion/switch auction result, an underwriting auction for ₹33,000 crore of government securities on 27 November, and Money Market Operations as on 25 November. **No rule, direction or circular is on that block.** The RBI's notifications list has its newest block also at 26 November: **two amendments to the UNSC's 1267/1989 ISIL (Da'esh) & Al-Qaida Sanctions List under Section 51A of UAPA — one entry, and 81 entries** — sanctions-list maintenance binding regulated entities for customer screening, a KYC obligation and not a lending rule; the rules report scopes them. SEBI's circulars listing, read 07:02 IST, still carries **25 November as its newest date** — the two circulars already covered, the 'Significant Indices' review and the KRA on-boarding circular in force 24 December 2026; **no circular dated 26 or 27 November was listed.** IBBI's "What's New" carries one 26 November item: **Shri Rahul Madan takes charge as Chairperson of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India** — a personnel fact, not a rule; the items below it are resolution-plan approvals dated 25, 23 and 16 November.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none today; the operative rulebook is unchanged, and today's AGLOC block is a market print inside it, not a rule move.

## 🏢 Muthoot Fincorp in the market

### The investor page re-read: 873 documents, unchanged; one e-auction notice out, one in — a rotation, not a filing
Muthoot Fincorp's investor page was re-read through the gated route at 07:02 IST (HTTP 200, 2,770,333 bytes) and shows **no new filing seen: 873 distinct document names — deduplicated on the S3 basenames — unchanged from 26 November**. The byte length differs by −36 bytes and is not a filing signal: presigned S3 signatures are baked at page-build time, so byte differences inside the cache window are expected; **the name-set diff is the reliable test, and it shows one e-auction notice out and one in** — `Auction_Notice_291026_c2504189fb.pdf` removed, `e_auction_8f26c13ce8.pdf` added. Both sit in the page's "E Auction Notice" section, one of three notice blocks alongside "Notice to Physical NCD holders" and "Joint Public Notice", and the 27 November page carries one of each.

Read honestly: **one e-auction notice out and one in, on the same count, is a notice rotation as notices are served and expire — not a new corporate filing, and it is not reported as one.** The rotation lands on the day ET reports legal auction notices going out across the industry; the coincidence is noted and nothing is drawn from it — **no count of notices served by any named company is in any public document, and none is asserted here.** "No new filing seen" is the phrasing, never "nothing was filed": the announcements list is partly loaded by script, and an item could still post later in the day.

The EGM trail is unchanged and still unreadable: the **proceedings of the EGM held on 23 November 2026 and the intimation of that meeting are on the page, named, and their contents are not readable from here** — the presigned links carry a 900-second expiry fixed at page-build time (this morning's carry X-Amz-Date=20261127T012142Z) and have expired. This edition reports that the documents exist, with their names and dates, and nothing more. An EGM's business could be borrowing limits, preference shares, director appointments or the IPO; guessing which would be fabrication, and none is attempted.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none asserted. The proceedings document is the authority on what the EGM resolved; until it is readable, the meeting is recorded here only as held, with its papers posted and unreadable.
Sources: [Muthoot Fincorp investor page, re-read 27 Nov 07:02 IST](https://www.muthootfincorp.com/investors)

### Muthoot Microfin's postal ballot on transacting with its holding company runs to 13 December
The direction of this filing is easy to misread, so it comes first: **Muthoot Microfin is the listed subsidiary seeking member approval to transact with Muthoot Fincorp Limited, its holding company. The parent is the related party in the notice, not the filer — this is not a Muthoot Fincorp filing, and neither company is Muthoot Finance.** The primary text is NSE-filed and fully readable: the postal-ballot notice dated 13 November 2026 and a corrigendum dated 25 November 2026.

The item: **material related-party transactions with Muthoot Fincorp for an aggregate value not exceeding ₹2,500 crore over one year, with no individual transaction above ₹500 crore**. The components named: **direct assignment of gold loans up to ₹2,000 crore; co-lending for gold loans; gold-loan customer sourcing and referral to MFL; gold custody at MFL's locker facility; commission on a ₹50 lakh bank guarantee; and cash management services through MFL branches.** Muthoot Microfin's FY26 standalone turnover is ₹2,369.56 crore, against a 10% materiality threshold of ₹236.96 crore. The 25 November corrigendum corrected the explanatory statement's financial-performance table, which had stated "₹ in Crores" instead of "₹ in Millions", and a typographical omission.

The clock: **remote e-voting runs from 09:00 IST on Saturday 14 November 2026 to 17:00 IST on Sunday 13 December 2026**, cut-off date 6 November 2026, **results on or before 17:00 IST on Tuesday 15 December 2026**. The shares closed at **₹164.45 on 26 November, up 3.53%** (NSE bhavcopy).

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: the ballot governs the assignment and co-lending arrangements the two companies use; the result is not known from here and is not predicted, and the e-voting window runs to 13 December.

reports.content:
# 📋 NBFC Regulatory Daily Report
**Date:** Friday, 27 November 2026 (IST)

Friday edition for 27 November 2026 (IST), covering Thursday 26 November to Friday morning; regulator pages read 07:02–07:03 IST. **Nothing dated 26 or 27 November changes a rule that applies to Muthoot Fincorp's lending business.** The RBI's newest press-release block is dated 26 November and carries only liquidity operations and statistical releases — VRR auctions, Reserve Money and Money Supply, a conversion/switch auction result, an underwriting auction and Money Market Operations — no rule. Its newest notification block is also dated 26 November and carries two UAPA sanctions-list amendments under Section 51A — one entry amended, and 81 entries — a customer-screening obligation, not a lending rule. SEBI has no circular dated 26 or 27 November; its newest remains the 25 November pair, both already covered in yesterday's edition. IBBI's 26 November item is the appointment of Shri Rahul Madan as Chairperson — a personnel fact, not a rule. What follows: the UAPA items scoped plainly and not inflated, the standing LTV bands with AGLOC's fresh 27 November block — a rise of ₹124 at the 85% band — what was checked, the latest circulars list, and the open deadlines.

---

## 🔔 New Regulatory Updates Today

The one-line position: **nothing new binds the company's lending business today.** The two newest instruments on any regulator's list are the RBI's UAPA sanctions-list amendments — real notifications, and their reach is customer screening, not lending. Everything else on the 26 November blocks is operations, statistics or personnel.

### RBI: two UAPA sanctions-list amendments under Section 51A — a screening obligation, not a lending rule
The RBI's notifications listing, read 07:02 IST, carries a newest block dated **26 November 2026** with two items on the same subject: **"Implementation of Section 51A of UAPA, 1967: Updates to UNSC's 1267/1989 ISIL (Da'esh) & Al-Qaida Sanctions List: Amendment of 01 Entry"**, and the same heading with **"Amendment of 81 entries"**. Both are sanctions-list maintenance under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act: the amendments add to and amend entries on the UNSC's consolidated sanctions list, and regulated entities are bound to screen customers and transactions against the updated list. **That is the whole of their reach — a KYC/screening obligation update. They do not change any gold-loan rule, any LTV band, any auction practice, any pricing norm or any other lending obligation, and this report does not inflate them into one.** No reference number for either notification is visible in the listing read this morning, so none is stated here.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: the company screens customers like any RBI-regulated entity, and an updated sanctions list is an input to that screening; no lending rule applying to the company changed today.
Sources: [RBI notifications, 26 Nov 2026 block](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx)

## 📖 The standing rulebook: the LTV bands, unchanged; AGLOC's 27 November block rises
The gold-loan LTV bands that Thursday's auction-notice reporting rests on are the standing ones: **85% for loans up to ₹2.5 lakh, 80% for loans between ₹2.5 and 5 lakh, 75% above ₹5 lakh.** **No RBI instrument dated 26 or 27 November changes them, and no instrument of any regulator dated those days changes any other rule applying to Muthoot Fincorp's lending business.** What did move is the published ceiling inside the bands: **AGLOC's block dated 27 November 2026 puts the bands at ₹9,548 a gram at 85%, ₹8,987 at 80% and ₹8,425 at 75%, on a jewellery reference of ₹11,233** — against the 26 November block of ₹9,424 / ₹8,869 / ₹8,315 on a reference of ₹11,087, that is **+₹124, +₹118 and +₹110, with the reference up ₹146** — the second rise in the series since 17 November, after the one on 24 November, against the falls recorded on 19, 20, 21, 23 and 26 November. The reference is fresh, not carried forward: **₹11,233 is IBJA's 26 November PM 916 rate ÷ 10 (11,233.9)**, so today's block rests on Thursday afternoon's bullion print exactly as the 26 November block rested on the 25 November one. **All three bands move together because they are fixed percentages of the one reference — one observation, not three** — and the percentages on those changes are arithmetic on AGLOC's own two blocks, because the page states rupee figures only.

One representation sits next to the bands today and is not a rule: the Economic Times reported on 26 November that **banks and gold-loan companies such as Muthoot and Manappuram have informed the RBI that, as a prudential measure, they have lowered the LTV on fresh loans to an average of 60–65% from about 75%.** ET names "Muthoot" without saying which entity — Muthoot Finance is the listed company, and Muthoot Fincorp is not named — and a representation to the RBI is not a rule change: **the bands stand, and lenders writing below them is prudential discretion, not a regulatory requirement on any named company.** It is written here as reported, not as a rule.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: these bands and this reference govern the ceiling the company lends under — ₹9,548 at the 85% band today, ₹124 higher than yesterday's. The fresh reference is a market print, not a rule move; the 60–65% figure is an industry representation reported by ET, not an obligation; and nothing in either changes the company's rulebook today.

## What was checked

The RBI's press-release listing was read at 07:02 IST on 27 November (HTTP 200, 161,584 bytes) and its newest block is dated **26 November 2026**, carrying eight items, every one of them a liquidity operation or a statistical release: a 3-day Variable Rate Repo auction under LAF on 27 November; Reserve Money and Money Supply for the fortnight ended 15 November; the result of the First Conversion/Switch Auction of State Government Securities; an Underwriting Auction for the sale of Government Securities for ₹33,000 crore on 27 November; the result of the Second Overnight Variable Rate Repo auction held on 26 November; the announcement of that Second Overnight VRR auction under LAF on 26 November; the result of the Overnight Variable Rate Repo auction held on 26 November; and Money Market Operations as on 25 November — **none a rule, a direction or a circular, and nothing on the block changes any rule applying to a gold-loan NBFC**; the 23 November block below it carries the items already covered in earlier editions — the Governor's meeting with the MDs and CEOs of select NBFCs, HFCs and industry representatives in Mumbai on 23 November, the same meeting with urban co-operative banks, the Sovereign Gold Bond premature-redemption price, the auction of GoI dated securities, the Reserve Bank (Securitisation Transactions) Amendment Directions, 2026, the draft Amendment Directions on preventive safeguards for electronic banking transactions, and the 2026 D-SIB list. The RBI's notifications listing, read at 07:02 IST (HTTP 200, 124,207 bytes), carries its newest block also at **26 November 2026** — the two UAPA sanctions-list amendments scoped above, amending one entry and 81 entries — with the 23 November block below it holding the four parallel securitisation amendment directions for All India Financial Institutions, NBFCs, Small Finance Banks and Commercial Banks; the NBFC one is the operative text for an NBFC and takes effect 1 April 2027, already covered in the 23 November edition, and a note on reading them: four near-identical instruments filed by lender class invite the error of reading one and concluding it does not apply — for an NBFC, the NBFC one is the operative text. SEBI's circulars listing was read at 07:02 IST (HTTP 200, 45,839 bytes) and its newest entry remains **25 November 2026** — the two circulars already covered in the 26 November edition, the half-yearly review of 'Significant Indices' and the simplification of client on-boarding at KYC Registration Agencies, which is in force 24 December 2026 — with **no circular dated 26 or 27 November listed**; SEBI's public-issues processing-status page returned HTTP 200 with only 6,035 bytes of navigation chrome, its table loading dynamically with no "As on" figure and no PDF link in the served HTML, so no processing figure is asserted from it; and the retired `legal/circulars.html` path returns HTTP 404 and is not cited. IBBI's homepage was read at 07:03 IST (HTTP 200, 1,612,379 bytes): its "What's New" carries the **26 November 2026** item "Shri Rahul Madan takes charge as Chairperson of Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India" (PDF, 79.51 KB) — a personnel fact, not an instrument — with the items below it resolution-plan approvals dated 25, 23 and 16 November, routine orders and not regulations; **no new IBBI regulation, circular or discussion paper dated 26 or 27 November was seen.** Nothing dated 27 November had posted on any of these pages at the 07:02 read — the normal state for a morning edition, the day being young.

latest_circulars.title: The next scheduled decision: the MPC meets 2–4 December
latest_circulars.summary: The Monetary Policy Committee meets on 2–4 December 2026, with the decision due on 4 December . The policy repo rate stands at 5.50% , raised 25 basis points at the 5–7 October meeting, with the stance changed to calibrated tightening; SDF 5.25%, MSF and Bank Rate 5.75%.
